lines.trans: Maybe the black-bean noodle portion was huge today—my stomach feels stuffed.
Mine is not digesting either—should we grab a soda or something?
Where are you two coming back from—you have not eaten lunch yet, right?
Let's hurry over and eat—they say today's staff cafeteria special is black-bean noodles!
We cannot leave the stage unattended—I will stay behind and guard the stage, so go enjoy lunch, Director!
Moments like this really show what a strong sense of responsibility Tae-ho has!
No really, do not worry about me—go escort the director to lunch!
What—do you not want to eat lunch with me?
Oh no, sir—not at all!
As a matter of fact I was craving black-bean noodles—let's head over!

meanings.note: The present day; often used adverbially without a particle.

examples.trans: The weather is nice today.
What day of the week is it today?
Did you hear about this black-bean noodles?
I was busy today because of black-bean noodles.

examples.text: 오늘 짜장면 양이 좀 많았나, 더부룩하다.
examples.trans: Maybe the black-bean noodle portion was huge today—my stomach feels stuffed.
Here the word for 'portion size' is key.
Please give me some water.
Please wait just a moment.

meanings.en: to be many, numerous, or abundant
meanings.note: Used for both countable and uncountable nouns.

examples.trans: Because it's the weekend, there are many people at the department store.

examples.text: 오늘 해야 할 일이 너무 많다.
examples.trans: There is too much work to do today.

examples.text: 오늘 짜장면 양이 좀 많았나, 더부룩하다.
examples.trans: Maybe the black-bean noodle portion was huge today—my stomach feels stuffed.
This expression comes from 'feels bloated and heavy'.

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.

examples.text: 나도 소화 안 되는데 콜라라도 먹어야 되나?
examples.trans: Mine is not digesting either—should we grab a soda or something?
Here the word for 'digestion' is key.

meanings.note: Short-form negation placed directly before verbs and adjectives

examples.trans: I'm not going to the office today.
I haven't watched that movie yet.

meanings.note: Takes a complement marked with 이/가.

examples.trans: I want to become a doctor.
It has already become 12 o'clock.

examples.text: 나도 소화 안 되는데 콜라라도 먹어야 되나?
examples.trans: Mine is not digesting either—should we grab a soda or something?
Here the word for 'even a cola' is key.

meanings.note: Everyday verb for eating a meal or food; honorific equivalent is 드시다.

examples.trans: Let's eat lunch together.
Did you eat breakfast?
Did you hear about this you guys?
I was busy today because of you guys.
Where is the restroom?
Where are you right now?

meanings.note: Basic verb of motion. With the respectful ending -세요 in 안녕히 가세요, it forms the polite farewell 'Goodbye!'. RR: gada.

examples.trans: I am going home.
Go safely!

meanings.en: to come (of a feeling, state, or weather)
meanings.note: Used in expressions like 혼란이 오다 (confusion comes) or 비가 오다 (rain falls)

examples.text: 한국에 온 지 일 년 됐어요.
examples.trans: It's been one year since I came to Korea.
I suddenly started feeling sleepy.

meanings.note: By extension, refers to a meal in everyday expressions like 밥 먹다 ('to eat a meal').

examples.trans: Have you eaten?
Today's lunch is delicious.
He hasn't come yet.
I still don't know.

meanings.note: commonly used when urging someone to act

examples.trans: We're late, so let's leave right away.
Come inside quickly before you catch a cold.

examples.text: 얼른 가서 밥 먹고 오자, 오늘 구내식당 특식 짜장면이래!
examples.trans: Let's hurry over and eat—they say today's staff cafeteria special is black-bean noodles!
Here the word for 'company cafeteria' is key.

examples.text: 얼른 가서 밥 먹고 오자, 오늘 구내식당 특식 짜장면이래!
examples.trans: Let's hurry over and eat—they say today's staff cafeteria special is black-bean noodles!
Here the word for 'special dish' is key.

meanings.note: a musical or show performance on stage

examples.trans: We have lots of stages that day.
Today's stage performance was really great.

examples.text: 무대를 비워둘 순 없죠, 무대는 제가 지킬 테니까 다녀오세요 국장님!
examples.trans: We cannot leave the stage unattended—I will stay behind and guard the stage, so go enjoy lunch, Director!
This expression comes from 'leave unattended'.

meanings.note: Bound noun used in -(으)ㄹ 수 있다/없다 ('can / cannot').

examples.trans: I can read Korean.
I cannot go today.

없다.gloss: to not exist, to not have

meanings.en: to not exist, to not be present

examples.trans: I don't have time right now.
The tickets are all sold out, so there aren't any.

meanings.note: Humble first-person singular pronoun used in polite speech.

examples.trans: I have an induction ceremony.
Follow me.

examples.text: 무대를 비워둘 순 없죠, 무대는 제가 지킬 테니까 다녀오세요 국장님!
examples.trans: We cannot leave the stage unattended—I will stay behind and guard the stage, so go enjoy lunch, Director!
This expression comes from 'guard'.
Did you hear about this since I intend to?
I was busy today because of since I intend to.

examples.text: 무대를 비워둘 순 없죠, 무대는 제가 지킬 테니까 다녀오세요 국장님!
examples.trans: We cannot leave the stage unattended—I will stay behind and guard the stage, so go enjoy lunch, Director!
This expression comes from 'please go and come back'.
Director-nim.
Director's office.

이러다.gloss: to do this, to act like this

meanings.en: to do this, to act like this

examples.trans: Why are you acting like this?
Please don't do this.

meanings.note: Often used as a bound noun after -(으)ㄹ to mean 'when' or 'while'.

examples.trans: Call me when you have time.
I lived in this neighborhood when I was young.

보다.gloss: to see, to watch; to take (an exam)

meanings.en: to see, to look at, to watch

examples.trans: I watched a movie on the weekend.
I took the driver's license exam.

meanings.note: 1st person plural pronoun; also used for 'my' with family, school, or workplace

examples.trans: Our team has a good atmosphere.
Let's eat lunch together tomorrow.

examples.text: 이 프로그램의 프로듀서인 본인은 무거운 책임감을 느낍니다.
examples.trans: As the main producer of this program, I feel a heavy sense of responsibility.
Here the word for 'sense of responsibility' is key.

meanings.note: used to emphasize an adjective or adverb

examples.trans: The food is really delicious today.
Time really flies.

examples.text: 이럴 때 보면 우리 태호가 책임감이 참 투철해!
examples.trans: Moments like this really show what a strong sense of responsibility Tae-ho has!
This expression comes from 'is rock-solid!'.

meanings.note: Negative copula used with nouns (often with -이/가)

examples.trans: It is not my fault.
Today is not Sunday, it's Monday.

괜찮다.gloss: to be fine; to be okay

meanings.en: to be fine; to be okay; to be alright
meanings.note: Used to reassure someone, decline an offer politely, or say something is acceptable.

examples.trans: I'm really fine.
Is it okay if we meet tomorrow?

examples.text: 다들 기다리고 계셔서 모시고 오라고 해서요.
examples.trans: Everyone is waiting, so they sent me to escort you over.

examples.text: 이번 일은 꼭 잘 해결해 봐요, 모시다는 마음으로요.
examples.trans: Let's make sure we handle this well (escort, accompany (humble)).
Why are you running?
Why were you late today?

meanings.note: Descriptive verb (adjective); the thing disliked takes the subject marker 이/가.

examples.trans: I really dislike rainy days.
You hate waking up early in the morning, right?

meanings.note: Expresses sudden realization, surprise, or hesitation.

examples.trans: Ah, yes.
Oh, I see!
No, I'm okay.
No, I haven't eaten yet.

그러다.gloss: to say so; to do so

meanings.en: to say so; to speak like that
meanings.note: contracted from 그러하다; often follows quoted speech

meanings.en: to do so; to act like that

examples.trans: Who said that?
That friend also said they are going together.
Oh no, sir—not at all!
Here the word for 'how could that possibly be!' is key.

meanings.note: Auxiliary adjective attached to a verb stem with -고 (-고 싶다).

examples.trans: I want to go to Korea.
I want to drink a cup of coffee.
Let's meet next time.
The next station is Seoul Station.
See you again!
It is raining again.

meanings.note: Action of coming together with someone.

examples.trans: I meet a friend.
Let's meet tomorrow.
